## Latent sync-echo risk (sibling of #201 / the payment echo, commit 1aefda4)

The 2026-06-30 HF Ville e2e surfaced a "write-back then sync re-imports as a
duplicate" bug for payments (fixed: `sync/mappers/payment.rs` now dedups on
`legacy_receipt_no OR pay_reference`). A scan of the other write-back entities
found **`ht_cash_ledger` carries the same class of risk**: the sync importer's
dedup key is not the column our writeback stamps the legacy id into, so when our
app originates a cash entry and mirrors it to legacy, the CT re-import would
insert a phantom duplicate (`pay_created_by`/source = `legacy_app`).

**Why it isn't biting yet:** cash-OUTBOUND writeback is still **dark** (unwired,
pending byte-shape verification — see the coexistence audit). So our app doesn't
originate cash entries into legacy today, hence no echo. But the moment cash
outbound is enabled, this will double-count the canonical cash ledger.

**Safe (check-ins are the reference pattern):** check-ins / bookings / POS sales /
coupons all dedup on the same column their writeback stamps, so they don't echo.

## Fix (before enabling cash-outbound writeback)
Mirror the payment fix: make the cash-ledger importer dedup on the column our
writeback stamps the legacy id into (or fall back to it), ordered to prefer the
app-authoritative row. Add an integration test for the round-trip.

Refs: commit 1aefda4, the payment-sync-echo workflow sibling scan.

## Why this matters

Stellar's actual differentiator versus every EVM chain is **anchors** — regulated, standardized fiat on/off-ramp and cross-border payment rails (SEP-6/24/31). Almost every general-purpose wallet treats this as an afterthought or skips it entirely, forcing users out to a separate exchange/app just to turn cash into XLM/USDC and back. A wallet with a first-class, integrated "Cash in / Cash out" flow plays directly to what Stellar is actually *for* (real-world payments, remittances), instead of competing generically on "yet another wallet that holds tokens.

## Current state (confirmed in code)

- Zero SEP-1/6/10/24/31 or "anchor" references exist anywhere in `src/` (grepped the full source tree).
- `src/core/session/handler.ts`'s `SIGN_AND_SUBMIT` **always submits to Horizon** — SEP-10 web authentication needs a **sign-only** path (sign a challenge transaction, return it, never submit it).
- The mini-app browser (`src/popup/screens/Apps.tsx`) already has a working **sandboxed overlay + iframe browser** (`Browser` component) with framing-blocked detection and an "open in new tab" fallback — this is directly reusable for hosting an anchor's SEP-24 **interactive** deposit/withdraw web flow, which is normally just a URL a wallet opens in a webview/iframe. Significant infra reuse, not a from-scratch feature.
- `src/core/stellar/client.ts` already has a network-aware Horizon client — the pattern (per-network base URLs, error handling) extends naturally to per-anchor TOML/API discovery.

## Confirmed: depends on #23's sign-only primitive

The sign-only (sign-but-don't-submit) message path needed for SEP-10 challenge signing is **owned and built by #23** (guardian recovery), which needs it first for guardian co-signing. This issue reuses that primitive rather than building its own — sequence this issue's SEP-10 work after #23's sign-only path lands, or coordinate closely if worked in parallel.

## Confirmed: target Testnet anchor left unspecified

The acceptance criteria requires demoing against "at least one real Testnet anchor" — **no specific anchor is locked in**; whoever implements this picks a currently-working Testnet anchor with SEP-24 support at implementation time (checking the Stellar anchor directory, since availability/uptime of test anchors changes).

## Proposed scope (SEP-24 first — it's the modern, most widely supported path)

### 1. SEP-1 discovery
Fetch and parse an asset issuer's `stellar.toml` (`https://<domain>/.well-known/stellar.toml`) to discover `WEB_AUTH_ENDPOINT`, `TRANSFER_SERVER_SEP0024`, and `SIGNING_KEY`.

### 2. SEP-10 web authentication
- Request a challenge transaction from the anchor's auth endpoint.
- **Sign it (do not submit)** — using the sign-only path built in #23.
- Return the signed challenge to the anchor, receive a JWT for subsequent SEP-24 calls.

### 3. SEP-24 interactive deposit/withdraw
- `GET /info` — discover which assets (start with **XLM and USDC**) the anchor supports for deposit/withdraw, and any limits.
- `POST /transactions/deposit/interactive` or `/withdraw/interactive` → anchor returns an interactive URL.
- **Open that URL in the existing sandboxed `Browser` overlay** (reuse, not rebuild) — the anchor's own hosted UI handles KYC/payment details; Lantern just hosts it and tracks the result.
- Poll `GET /transaction` (by id) for status updates (`pending_user_transfer_start`, `completed`, etc.) and surface progress/completion in the wallet — ideally folded into the existing Activity/history view (`src/core/history/`) so a deposit/withdraw reads like any other Stellar activity, not a separate silo.

### 4. UX entry point
A **"Cash in / Cash out"** action (Assets screen or its own tab) that:
- Lists a small **curated set of anchors** for the demo (mirroring the existing `core/miniapps/directory.ts` curation pattern — verified/vetted entries, not an open free-for-all) supporting XLM/USDC.
- Walks the user through SEP-10 auth → SEP-24 interactive flow → status tracking, with balance auto-refresh on completion.

### 5. Safety
Any transaction the anchor asks the user to sign as part of the flow (e.g. the actual deposit-completing payment) goes through the **existing scan engine** first, same as every other signature in the wallet — an anchor integration doesn't get a bypass lane.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] SEP-1 TOML discovery + parsing, unit-tested against a fixture TOML.
- [ ] SEP-10 challenge-sign-only flow implemented (via #23's sign-only primitive) and unit-tested (challenge validation: correct `SIGNING_KEY`/domain checks, so a malicious "anchor" can't trick the wallet into signing something else — the challenge tx itself must be validated, not blindly signed).
- [ ] SEP-24 `/info`, interactive deposit, interactive withdraw, and `/transaction` polling implemented against at least one real Testnet anchor (picked at implementation time — not fixed in this issue).
- [ ] Interactive flow renders inside the existing sandboxed `Browser` overlay (reuses #11/#12's infra) rather than a new webview implementation.
- [ ] Deposit/withdraw transactions are scanned before signing, same as any other transaction.
- [ ] Completed deposit/withdraw shows up in Activity/history and the balance refreshes.
- [ ] End-to-end Testnet demo: cash in some XLM or USDC via a real anchor, see it land in the wallet; cash out and see it complete.

## Out of scope (this issue)
- SEP-6 (non-interactive) — SEP-24 is the modern default; SEP-6 can be a follow-up if a target anchor requires it.
- SEP-31 (direct anchor-to-anchor payments, cross-border B2B rails) — bigger scope, separate issue if pursued.
- Anchor vetting/legal-compliance process for a production anchor list — Testnet-first, curated demo list only for v1.
- KYC data handling — that's entirely the anchor's own hosted interactive UI; Lantern never collects or stores it.
- Building the sign-only primitive itself — owned by #23, this issue only consumes it.

## Refs
- Reuses: `src/popup/screens/Apps.tsx` (`Browser` sandboxed overlay), `src/core/stellar/client.ts` (network-aware client pattern), `src/core/miniapps/directory.ts` (curation pattern), `src/core/history/` (activity feed).
- Cross-ref: #23 (owns and builds the sign-only-XDR primitive this issue depends on).
- Stellar docs: SEP-1 (stellar.toml), SEP-10 (web auth), SEP-24 (interactive deposit/withdraw).

## Problem
Speedcash still needs production-safe money state machines. Cash-in must not create spendable balance before trusted provider proof. Cash-out must use available/hold states and complete only after verified provider success.

## Risk
Unauthorized credits, misstated funds, stranded holds, and failed settlement accounting.

## Files likely affected
- `functions/src/transactions/handlers.ts`
- `functions/src/admin/handlers.ts`
- new Money Core service files
- provider adapter files
- state-machine tests

## Acceptance criteria
- Cash-in request creates pending provider-confirmation state only.
- Cash-in credit happens only after verified provider event or trusted status poll.
- Cash-out request reserves funds into hold state.
- Admin approval does not mark transaction complete.
- Provider success completes; provider failure reverses hold.
- All transitions are idempotent.

## Tests required
- Cash-in duplicate reference tests.
- Cash-in no-credit-before-proof tests.
- Cash-out hold/success/failure/reversal tests.
- State-transition unit tests.

## Bug description

The cash flow statement report (`GET /api/reports/cashflow-statement`) always
shows **$0.00** for "Cash at beginning of period" — and consequently a wrong
"Cash at end of period" — regardless of how much cash activity exists before
the report window. The operating/investing/financing sections compute
correctly; only the beginning/ending cash lines are wrong.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create any cash/bank transaction dated **before** the report window — e.g.
   a published manual journal dated 2025-12-31 debiting a bank account
   $10,000, or any earlier deposit.
2. Request the cash flow statement for a window starting after it:
   `GET /api/reports/cashflow-statement?from_date=2026-01-01&to_date=2026-12-31`
   (same result in the web UI).
3. "Cash at beginning of period" shows $0.00. Expected: $10,000.00.

The result is $0.00 for **any** `from_date` — the prior balance never appears.
Other reports (trial balance, balance sheet, general ledger) carry the same
prior balances forward correctly, so the data is fine; only this report's
beginning-cash line is affected.

## Root cause

The beginning-cash ledger is built from dateless SQL aggregation rows and then
filtered by date in memory, which drops every row:

1. `CashFlowRepository.cashAtBeginningTotalTransactions`
   (`packages/server/src/modules/FinancialStatements/modules/CashFlowStatement/CashFlowRepository.ts`,
   ~line 58) builds the query with the `creditDebitSummation` modifier —
   `SUM(credit), SUM(debit)` grouped by `accountId`, **no date column
   selected** (`packages/server/src/modules/Accounts/models/AccountTransaction.model.ts`,
   ~line 201). The date bound is applied here, in SQL
   (`filterDateRange(null, fromDate - 1 day)`), which is correct.

2. The resulting rows become a `Ledger` whose entries have `entry.date ===
   undefined` (`CashFlowService.ts` — `Ledger.fromTransactions(cashAtBeginningTransactions)`).

3. `CashFlow.cashAccountMetaMapper`
   (`packages/server/src/modules/FinancialStatements/modules/CashFlowStatement/CashFlow.ts`,
   ~line 379) then filters that ledger **again** by date:

   ```ts
   const closingBalance = this.cashLedger
     .whereToDate(cashToDate)   // <-- redundant; SQL already bounded the dates
     .whereAccountId(account.id)
     .getClosingBalance();
   ```

4. `Ledger#whereToDate` (`packages/server/src/modules/Ledger/Ledger.ts`, ~line 85):

   ```ts
   return this.filter(
     (entry) =>
       toDateParsed.isAfter(entry.date) || toDateParsed.isSame(entry.date),
   );
   ```

   With `entry.date === undefined`, both `moment#isAfter(undefined)` and
   `moment#isSame(undefined)` return `false` (comparison against an invalid
   moment), so **every** beginning-cash entry is filtered out and the closing
   balance is always 0.

## Suggested fix

Either:

- Remove the redundant `.whereToDate(cashToDate)` in
  `cashAccountMetaMapper` — the beginning-cash ledger is already bounded to
  `fromDate - 1 day` by `filterDateRange` in SQL; **or**
- Make `Ledger#whereToDate` retain undated entries
  (`entry.date == null || toDateParsed.isSameOrAfter(entry.date)`), since
  aggregated rows legitimately carry no date.

The first option is the smaller, more targeted change.

## Environment

- Self-hosted via Docker (`bigcapitalhq/server:latest`), current as of
  master `31c131a0` (NestJS server)
- Reproduced via both the REST API and the web UI
- Single-currency tenant (USD); transactions-locking disabled (defaults)

## Candidate high-value issue

Cash ledger truth remains only partially modeled. The relationship between transaction booking, settlement cash, projected cash, ledger cash, derived cashflows, and reconciliation status needs a governed contract.

## Evidence

- `docs/architecture/RFC-0083-target-state-gap-analysis.md` lists `Cash Ledger` as a partial baseline and says cash ledger truth needs clearer relationship to transaction booking, settlement, and reconciliation status.
- `docs/rfc-transaction-specs/shared/07-accounting-cash-and-linkage.md` requires every transaction RFC to define available cash, settled cash, projected cash, and ledger cash impact.
- The shared rule says no cash-side effect may exist without explicit linkage or documented external expectation.

## Why it matters

Private-banking workflows depend on cash availability and settlement correctness. If cashflows, cash balances, and transaction settlement are not governed as one source-truth model, downstream apps may double count, miss projected settlement, or confuse analytical performance cashflows with ledger cash.

## Suggested validation

- Define the canonical cash ledger/read model and its relationship to derived cashflows.
- Separate available, settled, projected, and ledger cash semantics.
- Ensure linked transaction/cash leg fields support reconciliation and explanation.
- Add tests for buys, sells, income, fees, transfers, FX, and settlement-date deltas.

## Acceptance criteria

- Cash ledger source truth is documented and exposed consistently.
- Cash-side effects are linked or explicitly marked external by contract.
- Reconciliation status is available where cash safety depends on it.

## Summary

Add a view-mode control on the **Spending** bar chart (`/charts/bar`) so users can switch between:

1. **Combined** — current behavior (bank + credit card together, stacked by budget).
2. **Cash & Credit** — side-by-side comparison per month (cash stack + credit stack, each broken out by budget).

Both modes keep the existing **budget → category → payee** drill-down flow.

## Problem

Combined spending hides whether a month was driven by card swipes vs checking debits. Users want to **compare** cash vs credit while still drilling into a budget the way the chart works today.

## Design (agreed)

### View control

Segmented control on the main chart card header:

| Mode | Label | URL |
|------|-------|-----|
| Default | **Combined** | omit param or `view=combined` |
| Compare | **Cash & Credit** | `view=split` |

Persist `view` alongside existing `?budget=` drill param (and `start`/`end` date range).

### Combined mode — unchanged

- One stacked bar per month, segments = budgets.
- Income line overlay (current behavior).
- Click budget (bar segment or legend) → category chart below → payee → transaction table.

### Cash & Credit mode — paired bars per month

For each month, two adjacent stacked bars:

```
         Jan              Feb
Cash    [budget stacks]  [budget stacks]
Credit  [budget stacks]  [budget stacks]
```

- Same budget colors and legend order as Combined mode.
- **Compare** cash vs credit height per month at a glance.
- **Income line:** keep the overlay in split mode (same month-level income series as Combined — not rail-specific).
- **Drill-down — two paths:**
  - **Bar segment click** → drill with **budget + rail** (`cash` | `credit`); category/payee/table filtered to that rail.
  - **Legend click** → drill **combined** budget totals (cash + credit together, no rail filter) — same as clicking a budget in Combined mode.

### Decisions (locked)

| Topic | Decision |
|-------|----------|
| Income line in split mode | **Keep it** — show in both Combined and Cash & Credit modes |
| URL param | `view=combined` (default) / `view=split` |
| Legend click in split mode | Drill **combined** budget (cash + credit); bar click drills single rail |

**Post-ship check:** After initial implementation, **prompt the operator to confirm** legend-click → combined drill feels right vs bar-only rail drill. Revisit if confusing in practice.

### Explicitly out of scope

- Three full-height charts stacked vertically (combined + cash chart + credit chart).
- Toggle that shows only Cash **or** only Credit (no side-by-side comparison).
- Cash Flow bar chart (`/cash-flow/charts/bar`) — different row population (`isCashFlowOutflow`).
- Removing or changing Combined mode defaults.

## Classification

| Rail | Filter |
|------|--------|
| Cash | `isSpendingWithdrawal` — asset withdrawal, not credit card |
| Credit | `isSpendingExpense` + `isCreditCard(source_type, source_role)` |
| Combined | `isSpendingExpense` (current) |

Edge cases (mislabeled card purchases on bank accounts) follow existing spending rules — no new heuristics in v1.

## Implementation notes

- Entry: `frontend/src/pages/SpendingBarPage.tsx` → `BudgetBarReportPage.tsx`.
- Chart: extend `SpendingBarChart.tsx` or add a split variant; ECharts grouped category axis for month × rail pairs.
- Data: extend `buildBarChartData` or add `buildSplitBarChartData` that returns cash + credit series per month.
- Drill: extend `BudgetReportDrilldown` row filter with optional `paymentRail: 'cash' | 'credit'` (omit for legend-click / combined drill).
- URL: read/write `view` query param; clear or preserve appropriately when date range changes (match `budget` reset behavior).
- Income line: render in both view modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Combined | Cash & Credit** control on Spending bar page; Combined is default.
- [ ] `view=combined` / `view=split` persisted in URL.
- [ ] Combined mode matches current chart and drill-down behavior.
- [ ] Cash & Credit mode shows paired cash/credit stacks per month, each stacked by budget.
- [ ] Income line visible in both modes.
- [ ] Split mode: bar click drills budget + rail; legend click drills combined budget.
- [ ] Tests cover row classification, split chart data building, drill filter with/without rail.
- [ ] Post-ship: operator prompted to confirm legend-click behavior (see Decisions).

## References

- `frontend/src/pages/SpendingBarPage.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/BudgetBarReportPage.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/SpendingBarChart.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/BudgetReportDrilldown.tsx`
- `frontend/src/lib/spending.ts` — `isSpendingExpense`, `isSpendingWithdrawal`
- `frontend/src/lib/accounts.ts` — `isCreditCard`

## Summary

On the **Receipts** screen, each calendar day already shows a single **Total** footer after the last receipt for that day (`ReceiptList.withDayTotals` in `core/`). Volunteers also need to see how much of that daily total was paid **cash** vs **card** — for end-of-day cash reconciliation.

Show a **Z-report style** breakdown under each day total: **Total**, then **Cash** and **Card** as indented sub-lines. Always show all three amounts, including `$0.00` when a payment method had no sales that day.

## User story

As a nursery volunteer reviewing the day’s sales on the Receipts screen, I want to see the total takings for each day and how much was cash vs card, so I can reconcile the cash drawer without mental arithmetic.

## Problem (current behaviour)

- `ReceiptListItem.DayTotal` carries only `totalCents`.
- `DayTotalRow` in `ReceiptsScreen.kt` renders one line: `"{date} Total: $X"`.
- Each `Receipt` already records `paymentMethod: PaymentMethod` (`CARD` / `CASH`) and the line totals are computed with `Money.receiptTotalCents`, but the day footer does not use payment method.

## Proposed behaviour

After the last receipt card for a calendar day, show a Z-report block (right-aligned, visually grouped):

```
3 July 2026
Total          $125.50
  Cash          $40.00
  Card          $85.50
```

Rules:

1. **Total** = sum of all receipts that day (unchanged — includes pending + exported, even when waterline grouping splits them).
2. **Cash** = sum of receipt totals where `paymentMethod == CASH`.
3. **Card** = sum of receipt totals where `paymentMethod == CARD`.
4. **Always show Cash and Card**, even when `$0.00`.
5. Cash and Card are **parts of** Total (not added on top). Visual hierarchy: date → Total (`titleMedium`, bold) → indented Cash/Card (`bodyLarge` or slightly lighter).
6. No backend / export / DB schema changes — `paymentMethod` is already persisted on receipts.

## Scope

### In scope

- `core/ReceiptList.kt`: extend `DayTotal` with `cashCents` and `cardCents`; compute in `withDayTotals`.
- `core/ReceiptListTest.kt`: tests for mixed days, all-cash, all-card, zero lines, pending+exported same day.
- `app/.../ReceiptsScreen.kt`: Z-report layout for `DayTotalRow`.

### Out of scope

- Per-receipt payment display changes (already on detail + confirm screens).
- Split-tender / partial cash+card on one receipt (not a domain concept today).
- Hiding zero payment-method lines.
- SQL aggregation in Room or logic in the ViewModel.

## Implementation sketch

### 1. `core/ReceiptList.kt`

```kotlin
data class DayTotal(
    val epochDay: Long,
    val totalCents: Long,
    val cashCents: Long,
    val cardCents: Long,
)
```

In `withDayTotals`, when grouping receipts by local calendar day:

- `totalCents` — existing sum over all receipts.
- `cashCents` — sum `Money.receiptTotalCents(lines)` for `paymentMethod == CASH`.
- `cardCents` — same for `CARD`.

Invariant: `cashCents + cardCents == totalCents` (only two payment methods exist).

### 2. `ReceiptsScreen.kt`

Replace single-line `DayTotalRow` with a small column: date label, Total row, indented Cash and Card rows using `Money.formatAud`. Match existing right-alignment and elderly-friendly typography (`Dimens`, `titleMedium` / `bodyLarge`).

### 3. Tests

Extend `receipt()` helper in `ReceiptListTest` with optional `paymentMethod`. Add cases:

- Mixed cash + card on one day → breakdown sums to total.
- All card → `Cash: $0.00`, `Card: $total`.
- All cash → opposite.
- Day split across pending/exported waterline → totals still sum all receipts on that day.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each day footer shows **Total**, **Cash**, and **Card** amounts.
- [ ] Zero payment-method days show `$0.00` for that method (not hidden).
- [ ] Cash + Card equals Total for every day block.
- [ ] Pending and exported receipts on the same day are all included.
- [ ] Business logic lives in `core/` with unit tests; UI only renders `ReceiptListItem.DayTotal`.
- [ ] `cd core && gradle test` passes.

## Verification

- `cd core && gradle test` (especially `ReceiptListTest`)
- No `app/` build required unless Compose layout tweaks need compile check

## References

- Day totals: `core/src/main/kotlin/com/nursery/core/ReceiptList.kt`, `ReceiptListTest.kt`
- UI: `app/src/main/java/com/nursery/scanner/ui/receipts/ReceiptsScreen.kt`
- Payment method on receipt: `core/src/main/kotlin/com/nursery/core/Models.kt`, `PaymentMethod.kt`
- Cart payment selection: `app/.../CartScreen.kt`

## The idea
A manager that keeps some dry powder: if cash drops below a floor, trim the largest positions until the floor is restored. Gives the buyers room to act and dampens full-invested risk.

## Signal
`cash_usd` and `total_value_usd` from `ctx.get_book()` → current cash as a % of NAV.

## Rule
When cash falls below `min_cash_pct` (default e.g. **5%**), trim the largest holding(s) proportionally until cash is back at the floor. When cash is already at/above the floor, do nothing (idempotent).

## Data
The book — nothing external.

## Copy this
[`sector_rebalancer.py`](https://github.com/tobyrowland/update_ai_analysis/blob/main/sector_rebalancer.py) is the closest pattern (a manager that computes targets and trades the deltas) with [`test_sector_rebalancer.py`](https://github.com/tobyrowland/update_ai_analysis/blob/main/test_sector_rebalancer.py).

## Context

Today's incident: a session got cancelled (weather — "too hot to go"). Of 3 affected students, one was refunded via the existing "Process Refund & Cancel" flow (`processRefund` in `src/actions/enrollments.ts:264`, wired to `enrollment-actions.tsx`'s refund dialog), but she'd have preferred credit toward a future Open Sailing session instead of cash back. Admin currently has no way to offer that.

## Decision (confirmed with Eric)

- **Admin-only, in-person.** No student-facing "request credit" self-service button — this is an admin judgment call made in conversation with the student, same trust model as the existing refund action.
- **Credit never expires.**
- Whether issuing credit *also* triggers a real Stripe refund (money leaves the school's Stripe balance) or is purely an internal ledger entry (school keeps the cash, student gets a redeemable balance) needs to be decided during implementation — see Open Questions. Andy's actual intent from the incident (she'd have taken credit instead of the refund) suggests the latter: no money moves, just a balance the student can apply later.

## Proposed approach

- New table (name TBD, e.g. `account_credits` or a running-balance column on `profiles` + a ledger table for audit trail — recommend the ledger table so credit issuance has a paper trail: who issued it, when, why, linked back to the originating `enrollment_id`/cancellation).
- New admin action alongside `processRefund` — likely `issueCredit(enrollmentId, courseId, amountCents)` in `src/actions/enrollments.ts`, admin-authorization-checked the same way `processRefund` is (`profiles.is_admin`).
- UI: a new action in `src/components/admin/enrollment-actions.tsx` next to the existing "Process Refund" `AlertDialog` — likely "Issue Credit & Cancel" following the same amount-entry pattern (`refundAmount` state, defaults to `payment.amountCents`, editable for partial credit).
- Cancels the enrollment the same way `processRefund` → `cancelEnrollment` does (flip attendance to `missed`, notify waitlist if a seat opened).
- No Stripe call for the credit path itself (assuming the "no money moves" interpretation above) — the `payments` row presumably needs a new status or a parallel record so admin views still show the original payment as accounted-for (not just silently unmodified while a credit floats separately).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Admin can issue account credit (full or partial amount) from the same screen/flow as "Process Refund," cancelling the enrollment.
- [ ] Credit amount, reason (linked enrollment/course), issuing admin, and timestamp are recorded — auditable later.
- [ ] Credit never expires.
- [ ] No student-facing UI to request credit — admin-initiated only.
- [ ] Admin can see a student's current credit balance somewhere (their profile, at minimum).

## Open questions

- Does issuing credit process an actual Stripe refund (money leaves Stripe) with credit as a *separate* promise to the student, or is it purely internal bookkeeping (no Stripe call, school keeps the cash)? Recommend the latter based on the incident's intent, but confirm before building.
- Does credit apply per-student only, or could a family/group need to share a pool? (Out of scope unless raised — assume per-student.)

## Related

- Enables #(this issue's redemption counterpart, filed separately) — applying credit balance at checkout.
- Shares a "settle a price difference" concern with the course-transfer feature (filed separately) — may be worth a shared primitive once both are scoped, not required to ship independently.

### Odoo Version

- [ ] 17.0
- [ ] 18.0
- [x] 19.0
- [ ] Other (specify)

### Steps to Reproduce

**Summary**
When closing a POS session, Odoo posts accounting entries in the following order:

Cash In/Out movements (e.g. daily cash withdrawals made during the session)
Aggregated sales revenue entries for the session

This means the cash journal temporarily shows a negative balance at the point where withdrawals are posted but session revenue has not yet been recorded. Although the balance corrects itself by the end of the closing process, the intermediate negative balance is written to the journal and visible in accounting reports and exports.

**Steps to Reproduce**

Open a POS session with a cash journal
Process several cash sales during the session
Use Cash Out (e.g. to withdraw the day's takings) during or at the end of the session
Close the session
Export or inspect the cash journal entries sorted by posting sequence

Result: The cash journal balance goes negative between the Cash Out entry and the subsequent revenue posting.
Expected: Sales revenue entries should be posted before any Cash Out entries, so the cash account balance never goes negative.

**Why This Matters – Legal Compliance (Germany / GoBD)**
Under German fiscal law (GoBD – Grundsätze zur ordnungsmäßigen Führung und Aufbewahrung von Büchern, Aufzeichnungen und Unterlagen in elektronischer Form), a cash register account must never show a negative balance. This is an explicit requirement that tax auditors check during a Betriebsprüfung (tax audit). A negative intermediate balance in the exported cash journal can lead to the entire cash accounting being rejected as non-compliant under §§ 146, 147 AO (Abgabenordnung).
This affects any German Odoo installation using POS with daily cash withdrawals – a very common operational pattern in retail and hospitality.

**Proposed Fix**

# Research Report: Agentic Quote-to-Cash & Proposal Engine

## 1. Problem Statement
Service-based small business owners and agency principals (e.g., Nora the Agency Principal, Carlos the Handyman) spend countless hours managing the quote-to-cash lifecycle manually. When a lead comes in, they must gather requirements, calculate estimates, draft a custom proposal in Word or specialized tools like Proposify, send it via email, wait for client approval, manually generate an invoice in Stripe or Quickbooks, and chase down payments. This fragmented workflow delays deal closures, increases administrative overhead, and frustrates non-technical users who want to focus on delivering their service. Existing CRMs and invoicing tools offer discrete solutions but fail to provide a unified, automated, end-to-end agentic workflow that actively moves the deal forward.

## 2. Research Report
- **Market Context**: Platforms like HoneyBook and Dubsado are popular among freelancers and small agencies because they combine proposals, contracts, and invoices. However, they rely entirely on the user to manually trigger the next step. Shopify focuses almost exclusively on product e-commerce and lacks native B2B or service quoting workflows.
- **The OHC Opportunity**: OneHumanCorp can differentiate itself by offering an "Agentic Quote-to-Cash Engine." By leveraging the Sales and Finance AI Agents, OHC can autonomously transition a lead from an initial inquiry into a drafted proposal, automatically convert an approved proposal into an invoice, and follow up on outstanding payments—requiring only one-tap approvals from the business owner.
- **Competitor Gaps**:
  - *HoneyBook / Dubsado*: Excellent workflow tools, but lack autonomous AI drafting and require heavy initial template setup.
  - *Shopify*: No native proposal or quoting mechanism for services; B2B features are gated behind enterprise tiers.
  - *Stripe Invoicing*: Powerful billing API, but lacks the upstream proposal drafting and negotiation interface.

## 3. Design Doc
### Data Model (PostgreSQL)
- `Lead`: The initial inquiry and customer details.
- `Proposal`: The drafted estimate, including line items, terms, and state (draft, sent, viewed, approved, rejected).
- `Invoice`: The final billable entity linked to the approved Proposal and integrated with Stripe.
- `Payment`: The record of the settled invoice.

### AI Agent Coordination
- **Sales Agent ("The Closer")**: Analyzes the initial Lead inquiry, queries the business's service catalog and pricing guidelines, and drafts a complete `Proposal`. It pushes a notification to the owner's mobile feed for approval.
- **Operations Agent ("The Manager")**: Monitors proposal states. Once a client approves the proposal online, it triggers the Finance Agent.
- **Finance Agent ("The Accountant")**: Automatically generates the `Invoice` from the approved `Proposal` line items, schedules it in Stripe, and drafts a payment request email. It also monitors for overdue payments and drafts polite follow-up reminders.

### Architecture Diagram
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Client Inquiry/Form] -->|Creates| B(Lead)
    B --> C[Sales Agent]
    C -->|Drafts| D[Proposal]
    D --> E{Owner Approval on Mobile}
    E -->|1-Tap Approve| F[Proposal Sent to Client]
    F -->|Client Accepts| G[Operations Agent]
    G -->|Triggers| H[Finance Agent]
    H -->|Generates| I[Invoice via Stripe]
    I --> J[Client Pays]
```

### Mobile UX Flow (375px First)
1. **Owner View (Agent Feed)**: The owner receives a card: "New inquiry from Acme Corp. Proposal drafted. [Review & Send]".
2. **Proposal Review**: The owner taps the card, viewing a clean, glassmorphism-styled summary of the drafted line items and total cost. They can edit fields or tap a large "Send Proposal" button (touch target ≥ 44x44px).
3. **Client View**: The client receives a beautiful, mobile-friendly web link to review the proposal, with a prominent "Accept & Sign" button.
4. **Post-Acceptance**: Once the client accepts, the owner receives another card: "Acme Corp accepted the proposal. Invoice drafted. [Send Invoice]".

## 4. Implementation Prompt
**Feature Name**: OHC Agentic Quote-to-Cash & Proposal Engine
**Target Persona**: Nora the Agency Principal
**Outcome**: Nora receives a project inquiry on her OHC site. The Sales Agent immediately drafts a proposal based on her standard rates. Nora approves it with one tap. When the client accepts the proposal, the Finance Agent automatically generates the invoice and schedules payment reminders, handling the entire workflow invisibly.

**Next Actions for Engineering**:
1. Implement the core Data Models (`Lead`, `Proposal`, `Invoice`) ensuring strict multi-tenant isolation.
2. Develop the Sales Agent capability to parse an unstructured inquiry and draft structured `Proposal` line items.
3. Build the mobile-first (375px) Proposal Review and Approval UI for the owner's Agent Feed.
4. Implement the client-facing Proposal Acceptance view.
5. Connect the Operations and Finance Agents to automatically transition an approved `Proposal` into a Stripe `Invoice`.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- The entire owner flow must be executable within a 375px viewport with no horizontal scrolling.
- The transition from Proposal to Invoice must require zero manual data entry from the owner.

**Priority**: P1
**Estimated Scope**: Large

✨Test end-to-end · Cash Management · date de valeur : le montant peut être juste, et le cash pourtant faux au mauvais moment.
Parce qu’en trésorerie, la vraie question n’est pas seulement “combien”, mais aussi “à partir de quand”.

En cash management, beaucoup d’équipes regardent d’abord la date comptable.
Mais la date qui change réellement l’effet du cash, c’est la date de valeur.
Le piège classique : un mouvement est bien visible, bien enregistré, bien réconcilié… mais il ne produit pas encore — ou ne produit plus — l’effet attendu sur la liquidité réelle.

🎯 En tant que Product Owner, je veux :
Un parcours qui distingue clairement date comptable, date d’exécution, et date de valeur.
Une Definition of Done qui impose “date de valeur visible et exploitable” sur les flux cash critiques.

🛠️ En tant que Developer, je veux :
Des règles côté serveur qui séparent correctement l’enregistrement du mouvement et son effet réel sur le cash.
Une traçabilité E2E : mouvement créé → date comptable → date de valeur → impact liquidité.

🙂 En tant que End User, je veux :
Comprendre à partir de quand le cash devient réellement utilisable ou impactant.
Ne pas confondre “visible dans l’outil” et “effectif en trésorerie”.

🛡️ En tant que QA, j’interviens afin de :
Définir un E2E “mouvement affiché → date comptable renseignée → date de valeur différente → impact cash correct”.
Tester les cas où les dates semblent proches mais changent la décision.
Exiger des preuves auditables : date comptable, date de valeur, règle appliquée, horodatage.

Votre point de rupture : vous pilotez la date visible… ou la date qui fait réellement foi sur le cash ?

📌 Zone technique.
Date comptable : date d’enregistrement du mouvement dans le système.
Date de valeur : date à partir de laquelle le mouvement produit son effet financier réel.
Preuves : dates, règle, impact liquidité, horodatage.

## Problem
The shared dual-leg accounting model requires position-level transactions with cash impact to have linked product and cash legs. The current model has linkage fields, but the pairing completeness and mismatch state should be persisted and queryable as first-class evidence.

## Evidence
- `docs/rfc-transaction-specs/shared/13-dual-leg-accounting-and-cash-adjustment-model.md` makes linked product/cash legs mandatory for BUY, SELL, DIVIDEND, INTEREST, and similar position-level transactions with cash impact.
- `Transaction` has nullable fields such as `economic_event_id`, `linked_transaction_group_id`, `originating_transaction_id`, `linked_cash_transaction_id`, `link_type`, and `reconciliation_key`.
- The same standard says a valid product leg without a corresponding cash leg is incomplete unless explicitly parked, and the same applies to a cash leg without a product leg.

## Why this matters
If product and cash legs are not paired deterministically, cash balances, performance flows, and reconciliation can double count or miss economic effects. Support teams also need to know whether a missing leg is expected, pending, rejected, or inconsistent.

## Suggested direction
- Add a pairing/economic-event ledger that records expected legs, received legs, matched legs, mismatch reasons, and completion state.
- Validate product/cash signs, net amount, currency, settlement account, and originating transaction links.
- Expose incomplete or mismatched pairs through supportability APIs.
- Treat parked incomplete pairs as a governed lifecycle state.

## Acceptance criteria
- Product/cash leg completeness is persisted per economic event or linked transaction group.
- Missing, duplicate, wrong-sign, wrong-currency, and wrong-account pairs are detectable.
- Tests cover engine-generated and upstream-provided cash leg pairing.
- Downstream cashflow and position processing can rely on pairing evidence.
